summary: This note is a wiki excerpt describing the structure and organization of the Canadian Armed Forces. It covers the Royal Canadian Navy's fleets and formations, the Armed Forces' three elements and reserve components, the command structure led by the Chief of the Defence Staff, and the Information Management Group's electronic warfare and cyber units. It closes by noting Canada's expanded international security role since the Cold War, especially in Afghanistan.
one_line: Overview of the Canadian Armed Forces' navy fleets, command structure, reserve components, and cyber/electronic warfare organization.
key_facts: The Royal Canadian Navy includes 33 warships and submarines deployed in two fleets.
Maritime Forces Pacific (MARPAC) is based at CFB Esquimalt on the west coast.
Maritime Forces Atlantic (MARLANT) is based at Her Majesty's Canadian Dockyard in Halifax on the east coast.
The Naval Reserve Headquarters (NAVRESHQ) is located at Quebec City, Quebec.
The Canadian Armed Forces consist of the Royal Canadian Navy, Canadian Army, and Royal Canadian Air Force.
The Reserve Force has four sub-components: the Primary Reserve, Supplementary Reserve, Cadet Organizations Administration and Training Service, and the Canadian Rangers.
Under the National Defence Act, the Canadian Armed Forces are an entity separate and distinct from the Department of National Defence.
The governor general appoints the Chief of the Defence Staff (CDS) on the advice of the prime minister.
The Armed Forces Council generally operates from National Defence Headquarters (NDHQ) in Ottawa, Ontario.
The Canadian Forces Information Operations Group is headquartered at CFS Leitrim in Ottawa.
In June 2011 the Canadian Armed Forces Chief of Force Development announced the Directorate of Cybernetics, headed by a Brigadier General, the Director General Cyber (DG Cyber).
The CAF Cyber Task Force was tasked within the Directorate of Cybernetics to design and build cyber warfare capabilities.
Since the end of the Cold War, NATO has moved much of its defence focus 'out of area', and the Canadian military has become more engaged in international security operations.
Canada's military has been deeply engaged in Afghanistan since 2002.
